fields.name: Tiger
fields.fun_fact: Tigers love water and are amazing swimmers! And guess what? Every tiger has its own unique stripe pattern!

fields.name: Emperor Penguin
fields.habitat: Antarctica and the surrounding Southern Ocean
fields.fun_fact: Emperor penguin dads keep their eggs warm on their feet! They huddle together in huge groups to stay warm during the freezing Antarctic winter.

fields.name: Komodo Dragon
fields.fun_fact: Komodo dragons are the largest living lizards in the world and can grow up to about 10 feet long! Even with their huge size, they can run surprisingly fast, up to around 12 miles per hour/19 kilometers per hour for short bursts.

fields.name: Cane toad
fields.fun_fact: Cane toads are some of the largest toads in the world and can grow about as big as a dinner plate! They also have special glands behind their eyes that help protect them from predators.

fields.name: Scarlet Skunk Cleaner Shrimp
fields.fun_fact: Why Arthropod? Because shrimp are crustaceans, and crustaceans belong to the arthropod group! Guess what? A shrimp’s heart is in its head area! That’s because its head and chest are joined together.

fields.name: Giant Manta Ray
fields.habitat: tropical, subtropical, and temperate oceanic waters
fields.fun_fact: Manta rays can grow wider than a car! Even though they are huge, they eat tiny plankton by filtering it from the water as they swim.

fields.name: Red Kangaroo
fields.habitat: Open scrublands, grasslands, and desert outback across mainland Australia
fields.fun_fact: When a red kangaroo joey is born, it is blind, hairless, and roughly the size of a jellybean or grape!

fields.name: Axolotl
fields.habitat: Freshwater lakes and canals in Xochimilco, Mexico
fields.fun_fact: Axolotls look like they're smiling, but their real superpower is even cooler! They can regrow lost legs and keep their fluffy-looking gills their entire lives!

fields.name: Green sea turtle
fields.habitat: Warm tropical and subtropical oceans worldwide
fields.fun_fact: Green sea turtles can sleep underwater for up to seven hours at a time without coming up for air!

fields.name: Pufferfish
fields.habitat: tropical and subtropical marine waters, with some species inhabiting brackish and freshwater
fields.fun_fact: A tiny male pufferfish spends a whole week flapping his fins to draw giant, seashell-decorated sand circles on the ocean floor to impress a mate!

fields.name: Monarch butterfly
fields.habitat: sunny fields and gardens with milkweed in the summer, and coastal or mountain forests in the winter.
fields.fun_fact: Monarch butterflies taste with their feet using special sensors that help them find sweet nectar and the right milkweed leaves to lay their eggs on

fields.name: Vampire Bat
fields.habitat: Americas, ranging from northern Mexico through Central America and down into South America
fields.fun_fact: Their diet consists 100% of liquid blood!

fields.name: Great horned owl
fields.habitat: Arctic down to South America, thriving in forests, deserts, prairies, mountains
fields.fun_fact: One of the most surprising facts about the Great Horned Owl is that it regularly hunts and eats skunks. Because these owls have virtually no sense of smell, a skunk's smelly spray does not bother them at all!

fields.name: Grey Wolf
fields.habitat: forests, mountains, tundra, taiga, and grasslands across North America, Europe, and Asia
fields.fun_fact: Every wolf has a completely unique howl! Much like a human fingerprint—which allows pack members to identify each other from miles away!
